t: Thebes was the largest and leading polis of the Boeotian League and was often called "Seven-Gated Thebes".
The Theban army trained and led by Epaminondas and Pelopidas defeated the Spartans at Leuctra in 371 BCE, beginning a short Theban hegemony.
After a revolt in 335 BCE Alexander the Great destroyed the city and sold the Thebans into slavery; Cassander re-established it in 315 BCE.
dyk: When Alexander destroyed Thebes in 335 BCE, tradition holds that he spared only the temples and the house of the poet Pindar, along with priests, the pro-Macedonian party and Pindar's descendants.
ev: During the Persian invasion of Greece the governing aristocracy of Thebes joined Xerxes I and fought for him at the Battle of Plataea
At the head of the Boeotian levy the Thebans defeated an Athenian army at the Battle of Delium
A Spartan force seized the Cadmea by a coup de main; it was expelled three years later and a democratic constitution set up
Theban forces under Epaminondas defeated the Spartans at the Battle of Leuctra
Epaminondas died at the Battle of Mantinea and Thebes sank back to a secondary power
Philip II of Macedon defeated Thebes and Athens at the Battle of Chaeronea
Alexander the Great destroyed Thebes after its revolt and sold its people into slavery
Cassander re-established Thebes with labour and money from other Greek cities

f.capital: Thebes, with its citadel, the Cadmea
f.founder: not known; Greek tradition named Cadmus, a Phoenician prince from Tyre
f.predecessor: The Mycenaean settlement of the Bronze Age at the Cadmea
f.successor: Roman rule after the Achaean War of 146 BCE; the Province of Achaia from 27 BCE
